title: A winding river can slice through its own bend and leave a lake behind
body: On a flat floodplain, a river swings from side to side. At every bend it eats sideways into the outer bank, while a current along the riverbed sweeps loose sand and silt towards the inner bank and drops it there, so each loop grows and drifts across the land. When two bends almost meet, the river breaks through the narrow neck between them, by erosion or in the strong currents of a flood, and takes the short cut. Sediment then seals off the abandoned loop, leaving a curved, still **oxbow lake** that can silt up into a swamp within a few years to several decades.

cover.alt: Satellite view of a wide brown river looping in tight S-shaped bends through dark green rainforest
cover.credit: NASA Scientific Visualization Studio · Public domain

slides.alt: Satellite images of a wide brown river winding through green rainforest, one per year from 1985 to 2023: its tight S-shaped bends swell, swing sideways and change shape, while old loops are left behind as curved lakes. Clouds come and go between frames.
slides.caption: Peru’s Ucayali River, one Landsat image a year from 1985 to 2023, slowed to about a third of the original speed: the bends swing and shift, and old loops are cut off as lakes.
slides.credit: NASA SVS, Ross K. Walter (SSAI) · Public domain · excerpt, cropped and slowed 3.3×

steps.label: The river swings into wide loops
It wears away the outer bank of each bend
It drops sediment on the inner bank
It breaks through the neck of a loop
The old loop is sealed off as a lake

left.label: Cut bank
left.text: The outer bank, with the wider curve: the river undercuts it and wears it away

right.label: Point bar
right.text: The inner bank, with the tighter curve: sand, silt and gravel pile up here

slides.heading: Match the word to its meaning
slides.explanation: Oxbow lakes have local names: billabongs in Australia and resacas along the Rio Grande in South Texas.

slides.question: With no current flowing through it, what usually happens to an oxbow lake?
options: It silts up into a bog or swamp
It turns salty like the sea
It grows into a new river
slides.explanation: Still water lets silt settle, so the lake bed slowly fills; it can become a bog or swamp and finally dry out, over a few years to several decades.
